_doc: Sourced US list prices (monthly, new subscribers) for evergreen price-history sections on service pages. date = YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD when the change took effect for new subscribers. Add rows only with a source.

Netflix.intro: Netflix has raised US prices roughly every one to two years since it split streaming from DVD rentals in 2011. Its main ad-free plan (Standard) has gone from $7.99 to $19.99 a month, and that plan has never gotten cheaper.

latest.what: all three US plans went up: Standard with ads $7.99 to $8.99, Standard $17.99 to $19.99, Premium $24.99 to $26.99. Extra members rose to $7.99 (with ads) and $9.99 (ad-free).

notes: Basic closed to new US members on July 19, 2023 and ended for remaining members on July 18, 2024.
The 2014 increase applied to new members first; existing members kept $7.99 for a period.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)
Dormant: streaming price history (dated flagship prices)

Spotify.intro: Spotify Premium Individual cost $9.99 a month in the US for twelve years, from its 2011 launch until July 2023. It has gone up three times since, and is now $12.99.

latest.what: Spotify announced US increases to Individual $12.99, Duo $18.99, and Family $21.99, with existing subscribers notified by email over the following month. Our own daily snapshot of spotify.com/us/premium shows these prices today.

notes: Family launched in 2014 at $14.99 for two people (more for extra members); in May 2016 it became $14.99 for up to six.
Student was $5.99 after both the 2023 and 2024 increases.

Disney+.intro: Disney+ launched in the US at $6.99 a month in November 2019. The ad-free plan is now $21.49, up more than 200%, with at least one price increase every year since 2022.

latest.what: ad-free Disney+ Premium went from $18.99 to $21.49 and Disney+ with ads from $11.99 to $12.49 for new subscribers; existing subscribers moved to the new price on their next monthly bill.

notes: The September 2026 change also raised the ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle from $19.99 to $21.99; the bundle with ads stayed at $12.99.
Disney+.title: Disney+ price change history (US, 2019–2026): every price increase, dated
faq_extra: What is the Disney+ price change history?

Ad-free Disney+ (now Premium) launched at $6.99 a month on November 12, 2019, then went to $7.99 on March 26, 2021, $10.99 on December 8, 2022, $13.99 on October 12, 2023, $15.99 on October 17, 2024, $18.99 on October 21, 2025 and $21.49 on September 23, 2026. Disney+ with ads launched at $7.99 on December 8, 2022, then went to $9.99 on October 17, 2024, $11.99 on October 21, 2025 and $12.49 on September 23, 2026. Dates are when new subscribers started paying the new price.

Hulu.intro: Hulu's ad-free plan launched at $11.99 a month in 2015 and is now $21.49, after five increases. The plan with ads, which Hulu cut to $5.99 in 2019, has since doubled to $12.49.

latest.what: Hulu (No Ads) went from $18.99 to $21.49 and Hulu with ads from $11.99 to $12.49 for new subscribers, with existing subscribers moving to the new rates at their next billing date. The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads stayed at $12.99.

notes: The 2010 rows are Hulu Plus, the paid ad-supported plan; Hulu's free ad-supported site ran separately until 2016.
Disney took full ownership of Hulu in 2025 and plans to fold Hulu's content into Disney+; bundle prices are not tracked here.
Hulu + Live TV is a separate product and not included in these tables.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)

Peacock.intro: Peacock has raised prices every summer since 2023. Its main plan, Premium (with ads), launched at $4.99 a month in July 2020 and is now $12.99, more than two and a half times the launch price.

latest.what: Premium went from $10.99 to $12.99, Premium Plus from $16.99 to $19.99, and Select from $7.99 to $8.99 a month for new subscribers. People who subscribed before Aug 18 moved to the new prices at their first billing date on or after Sep 17.

notes: Peacock's free tier closed to new members in 2023.
Select (launched July 2025) is a cheaper tier with NBC and Bravo shows but no movies, live sports or Peacock originals.
Annual plans also rose on Aug 18, 2026: Select $89.99, Premium $129.99, Premium Plus $199.99 a year.
sources: Streaming Price Tracker: US price history (per-change citations)

YouTube.name: YouTube Premium
YouTube.intro: YouTube's ad-free subscription launched as YouTube Red at $9.99 a month in 2015. Renamed YouTube Premium in 2018, the individual plan is now $15.99, and the family plan has gone from $17.99 to $26.99 since 2022.

latest.what: YouTube Premium Individual went from $13.99 to $15.99, Family from $22.99 to $26.99, and Premium Lite from $7.99 to $8.99 a month. New sign-ups paid the new prices right away; existing subscribers were emailed and moved over at a later billing date. The annual individual plan went from $139.99 to $159.99.

notes: The 2015 price is YouTube Red, which became YouTube Premium in June 2018.
Prices are for paying on YouTube's website; subscribing through Apple's App Store costs more.
Premium Lite removes most ads but doesn't include YouTube Music, background play or downloads.
sources: Ars Technica, Apr 2026 (Red and Premium launch prices)

Amazon Prime.intro: Amazon Prime launched at $79 a year in 2005 and now costs $139 a year or $14.99 a month. Amazon has raised the membership about every four years, most recently in February 2022, and has not announced an increase in 2026.

latest.what: Prime went from $119 to $139 a year and from $12.99 to $14.99 a month for new members. Ad-free Prime Video costs extra on top of that: $2.99 a month from January 2024, renamed Prime Video Ultra at $4.99 a month in April 2026.

notes: Amazon's help page lists today's prices: $14.99 a month, $139 a year, Prime Video alone $8.99 a month, Prime for Young Adults $7.49 a month or $69 a year.
Analysts have predicted a 2026 increase to about $159 a year; Amazon has not confirmed one.
sources: Amazon Customer Service: The Amazon Prime Membership Fee
Streaming Price Tracker: Prime Video history

HBO Max.intro: HBO Max launched in May 2020 at $14.99 a month with no ads. It became Max in May 2023 and HBO Max again in July 2025. The ad-free Standard plan is now $18.49, the 4K Premium plan $22.99, and the ad-supported plan $10.99, after the latest increase on October 21, 2025.

latest.what: HBO Max raised every plan: Basic with Ads from $9.99 to $10.99, Standard from $16.99 to $18.49 and Premium from $20.99 to $22.99 a month. New subscribers paid the new prices right away; existing monthly subscribers moved over at their first billing date on or after November 20, 2025.

notes: Plan names have changed with the brand: the ad-supported plan was HBO Max With Ads, then Max Ad-Lite, now Basic with Ads; Standard was the Ad-Free plan; Premium was Max Ultimate Ad Free, added when Max launched on May 23, 2023.
Max was renamed back to HBO Max on July 9, 2025, with no change to plans or prices.

After Paramount Skydance completed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison said on October 7, 2026 that HBO Max and Paramount+ will be run separately for now and combined over time. No price change for HBO Max has been announced.
Current prices from HBO Max's own plans page: Basic with Ads $10.99/month or $109.99/year, Standard $18.49 or $184.99, Premium $22.99 or $229.99, before tax.
sources: HBO Max help: plans and prices (current prices)
HBO Max help: price changes, Oct 2025 (annual prices, dates)
Warner Bros. Discovery, Apr 12, 2023 (Max launch prices)
TechCrunch, Jan 12, 2023 ($14.99 to $15.99, first increase since May 2020)
WBD Pressroom: HBO Max is back (Jul 2025)

HBO Max.title: HBO Max price increase history (US, 2020–2026): every price hike, dated
faq_extra: What is the HBO Max price increase history?

HBO Max's ad-free plan (now called Standard) launched at $14.99 a month in May 2020 and has gone up three times: to $15.99 on January 12, 2023, $16.99 on June 4, 2024 and $18.49 on October 21, 2025. The ad-supported plan (now Basic with Ads) went from $9.99 at its June 2, 2021 launch to $10.99 on October 21, 2025. The 4K Premium plan went from $19.99 at Max's May 23, 2023 launch to $20.99 on June 4, 2024 and $22.99 on October 21, 2025. Standard billed yearly went from $149.99 (May 2023) to $169.99 (June 2024) to $184.99 (October 2025).
Is HBO Max raising prices again?

No new standalone HBO Max increase had been announced as of October 26, 2026, and HBO Max's own plans page still listed $10.99, $18.49 and $22.99 a month that day. After Paramount Skydance's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery closed in October 2026, the company said HBO Max and Paramount+ will be combined over time, but it hasn't said what a combined service would cost.

Paramount+.intro: Paramount+ replaced CBS All Access on March 4, 2021, with an ad-free plan at $9.99 a month, and added a $4.99 ad-supported Essential plan that June. After three increases to each plan, Essential is $8.99 and the ad-free Premium plan is $13.99, both raised on January 15, 2026.

latest.what: Paramount+ Essential went from $7.99 to $8.99 and Premium from $12.99 to $13.99 a month. Annual plans rose more: Essential from $59.99 to $89.99 a year and Premium from $119.99 to $139.99.

notes: Premium was called Paramount+ with Showtime from June 27, 2023 (it replaced the $9.99 ad-free plan at $11.99) until 2025, when it was renamed Paramount+ Premium.
The $4.99 Essential plan replaced CBS All Access's $5.99 plan with commercials and, unlike it, left out live local CBS stations.
In August 2024, existing monthly Essential subscribers kept $5.99; the $7.99 price applied to new subscribers.

After Paramount Skydance completed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison said on October 7, 2026 that Paramount+ and HBO Max will be run separately for now and combined over time. No new Paramount+ price has been announced.
Current monthly prices ($8.99 Essential, $13.99 Premium) confirmed on paramountplus.com on October 19, 2026.

Apple TV.intro: Apple TV+ launched in November 2019 at $4.99 a month and was renamed Apple TV in October 2025. It has now gone up four times, most recently to $14.99 a month and $119 a year on August 28, 2026, three times its launch price.

latest.what: Apple TV went from $12.99 to $14.99 a month and from $99 to $119 a year, and Apple One Individual from $19.95 to $21.95. New subscribers paid the new price right away; Apple said existing subscribers would be notified about a month before being charged it.

notes: Apple dropped the plus and renamed Apple TV+ to Apple TV on October 13, 2025. Prices didn't change with the rename.
The annual plan stayed at $99 when the monthly price went to $12.99 in August 2025, then rose to $119 in August 2026.
Apple TV is also included in Apple One bundles, which start at $21.95 a month (Individual) as of October 2026.
Current $14.99 monthly price confirmed on apple.com on October 19, 2026.
sources: MacRumors, Oct 25, 2023 ($6.99 to $9.99, $69 to $99 a year)
The New York Times, Oct 13, 2025 (rename to Apple TV)

Slack.title: Slack pricing history (2014–2026): every Pro, Business+ and Enterprise+ price change
Slack.basis: US list prices per active user per month, before tax, in nominal dollars, for buying on Slack's website. Annual-billing prices are Slack's per-month equivalent. Compiled from the sources below and our daily snapshots of slack.com/pricing; last verified {verified}.
Slack.intro: Slack kept its Pro plan (originally called Standard) at $8 per user a month, or $6.67 billed annually, from its 2014 launch until September 1, 2022. Business+ went from $12.50 to $15 per user a month in 2025, when Salesforce folded AI features into it. Today Pro is $8.75 monthly or $7.25 annually, and Business+ is $18 monthly or $15 annually.

latest.what: Slack raised Business+ from $12.50 to $15 per user a month on annual billing, and from $15 to $18 on monthly billing, adding AI features and Salesforce integrations. Pro prices stayed the same. Business+ customers who bought on Slack's website moved to the new plan at their first renewal after August 17, 2025.

notes: The September 1, 2022 Pro increase was Slack's first since launching in 2014. Annual Pro customers could lock in $6.67 for another year by renewing before that date.
The same day, the Free plan switched from the last 10,000 messages and 5GB of files to the last 90 days of messages and files.

Enterprise+ was added in June 2025 as a contact-sales plan. Since October 15, 2026, Slack's pricing page has sometimes shown it at $45 per user a month and sometimes as 'Contact sales', which looks like a test (see our Slack changelog below).
Turning AI features off doesn't lower the price of a Slack plan, according to Slack's help center.
Enterprise Grid and contracts signed through Slack sales aren't covered here; pricing for those is negotiated.
sources: Slack blog, Jun 17, 2025 (Business+ $12.50 to $15; monthly $15 to $18)
Slack help: updates to feature availability and pricing (Aug 17, 2025 renewals)
The Verge, Jul 19, 2022 (Pro $8 to $8.75, $6.67 to $7.25; Free 90-day limit)

Audible.title: Audible price history (2020–2026): Premium Plus, Standard and Plus prices
Audible.desc: Audible US price history since 2020: Premium Plus has stayed $14.95 a month, the $7.95 Plus plan closed to new members on Mar 3, 2026, and Standard launched at $8.99. Dated tables, sources, and daily pricing-page tracking.
Audible.basis: US list prices for new members, before tax, in nominal dollars, from Audible's announcements, coverage linked below, and our daily snapshots of Audible's membership page; last verified {verified}. Introductory offers (such as Prime member trials or limited-time annual deals) are left out.
Audible.intro: Audible has not raised the price of its main plan in years: Premium Plus, with one credit a month, has been $14.95 since Audible renamed its Gold plan in August 2020, and Gold cost the same before that. What changed in 2026 was the cheapest way in. On March 3, 2026, Audible launched a $8.99 Standard plan and stopped selling the $7.95 Audible Plus plan to new members, so the lowest price a new customer can pay went up by $1.04, while existing Plus members kept their plan.

latest.what: Audible launched a Standard plan at $8.99 a month in the US (one audiobook a month that you can listen to while you stay a member, plus an unlimited catalog) and closed the $7.95 Audible Plus plan to new members. Premium Plus stayed at $14.95.

Audible.faq_last: Audible has not raised Premium Plus, which has been $14.95 a month since August 2020. The closest thing to an increase came on March 3, 2026, when Audible stopped selling the $7.95 Audible Plus plan to new members and launched an $8.99 Standard plan, so the cheapest plan for new members went from $7.95 to $8.99.
Audible.faq_up: Premium Plus has not gone up: it was $14.95 a month when it replaced Audible Gold in August 2020 and is still $14.95. The entry price for new members rose from $7.95 (Audible Plus) to $8.99 (Standard) on March 3, 2026.

Premium Plus (1 credit a month): Renamed from Audible Gold at the same price
Premium Plus (2 credits a month): Renamed from Audible Platinum at the same price
Premium Plus annual (12 credits): Earliest price on record we found; unchanged since
Premium Plus annual (24 credits): Earliest price on record we found; unchanged since
Plus (discontinued for new members): Closed to new members; existing members keep it

notes: Audible Plus launched in preview on August 24, 2020, with sign-ups for new customers starting August 27. The same day, Audible Gold and Platinum were folded into Premium Plus, keeping their prices.

Standard does not give credits. The Verge corrected its launch story to say so: you pick one audiobook a month and lose access to it if you cancel, unlike Premium Plus credits, which buy titles you keep.

Our daily snapshot of Audible's US membership page on October 21, 2026 shows Standard at $8.99 a month, Premium Plus at $14.95 a month, and annual Premium Plus at $149.50 and $229.50 a year. Since October 16, 2026, it has also shown a limited-time offer of $99 for a year of Premium.
sources: Audible newsroom, Aug 24, 2020 (Audible Plus and Premium Plus)
Duskalo Audible price history (annual plan prices on record since Jan 2022)

Xbox Game Pass.title: Xbox Game Pass price history (2017–2026): Ultimate from $14.99 to $29.99, now $22.99
Xbox Game Pass.desc: Every Xbox Game Pass US price change: Ultimate went from $14.99 (2019) to $29.99 on Oct 1, 2025, then Microsoft cut it to $22.99 on Apr 21, 2026. PC Game Pass, Premium and Essential too, plus the November 2026 cloud gaming hour limits. Dated and sourced.
Xbox Game Pass.basis: US list prices for new members, monthly, before tax, in nominal dollars, from Xbox Wire, Microsoft's US store listings and the coverage linked below; last verified {verified}. Introductory and targeted offers ($1 trials, win-back deals) are left out.
Xbox Game Pass.intro: Xbox Game Pass Ultimate cost $14.99 a month from its June 2019 launch until July 2023. Microsoft then raised it three times in a little over two years: to $16.99 in July 2023, $19.99 in July 2024 and $29.99 on October 1, 2025, a 50% jump in one step. On April 21, 2026, Microsoft reversed part of that, cutting Ultimate to $22.99 and PC Game Pass from $16.49 to $13.99, and said new Call of Duty games would join those plans about a year after launch instead of on day one. The next change is not a price: from November 2026, cloud gaming on every plan gets a monthly hour limit.

latest.what: Microsoft cut Game Pass Ultimate from $29.99 to $22.99 a month and PC Game Pass from $16.49 to $13.99, and said future Call of Duty games would join both plans about a year after launch rather than on day one. Premium ($14.99) and Essential ($9.99) did not change.

last_up.what: Xbox Game Pass Ultimate went from $19.99 to $29.99 a month and PC Game Pass from $11.99 to $16.49 (Microsoft cut them to $22.99 and $13.99 on Apr 21, 2026).

Xbox Game Pass.faq_last: The last increase was on October 1, 2025, when Ultimate went from $19.99 to $29.99 a month and PC Game Pass from $11.99 to $16.49. Since then prices have come down: on April 21, 2026, Microsoft cut Ultimate to $22.99 and PC Game Pass to $13.99. From November 2026, each plan also includes only a set number of cloud gaming hours a month (15 on Ultimate, 10 on Premium, 5 on Essential).
Xbox Game Pass.faq_up: Game Pass Ultimate launched at $14.99 a month in June 2019 and costs $22.99 today, up 53%. It rose to $16.99 in July 2023, $19.99 in July 2024 and $29.99 on October 1, 2025, then was cut to $22.99 on April 21, 2026.

Ultimate: New members first; existing members from Sep 12, 2024
PC Game Pass: Launch list price of Xbox Game Pass for PC (beta), sold at $4.99 a month as a limited-time launch offer
New members first; existing members from Sep 12, 2024
Premium (formerly Standard): Renamed Game Pass Premium at the same price; PC games and cloud gaming added
Essential (formerly Core): Renamed from Game Pass Core at the same price
for Console (discontinued for new member: Closed to new members; existing members could keep renewing

notes: Cloud gaming limits from November 2026: Xbox Wire said on September 3, 2026 that Ultimate will include 15 hours of cloud gaming a month, Premium 10 and Essential 5, with extra hours sold through the Xbox Store; Microsoft expects it to affect 4% of subscribers and said that "for some players the practical result is a higher cost." On October 21, 2026, Xbox Insiders got introductory cloud playtime packs at 10 hours for $3.99, 25 hours for $7.99 and 50 hours for $11.99.

Microsoft's US store listings on October 22, 2026 show Ultimate at $22.99 a month (prepaid: $68.99 for 3 months, $137.99 for 6 months, $275.99 for 12 months), PC Game Pass $13.99, Premium $14.99 and Essential $9.99 (12 months prepaid: $79.99).
In July 2024, Microsoft raised the 12-month Game Pass Core price from $59.99 to $74.99 while the monthly price stayed $9.99.
In September 2026, some lapsed and current members reported account-specific Ultimate offers below list price, such as $16.09 a month for 12 months; Microsoft still lists $22.99.
The October 2025 changes renamed Core to Essential and Standard to Premium and added Fortnite Crew and Ubisoft+ Classics to Ultimate.

PlayStation Plus.title: PlayStation Plus price history (2022–2026): Essential, Extra and Premium, every increase
PlayStation Plus.desc: PS Plus US price history since the June 2022 relaunch: 12-month plans rose by up to $40 on Sep 6, 2023, and 1- and 3-month plans rose on May 20, 2026 (Essential $10.99, Extra $16.99, Premium $19.99 a month). Dated tables and sources.
PlayStation Plus.basis: US list prices for new subscribers, before tax, in nominal dollars, from Sony's announcements, PlayStation's US PS Plus page and the coverage linked below; last verified {verified}. Sales and discounted upgrade offers are left out.
PlayStation Plus.intro: Sony has raised PlayStation Plus prices twice since it relaunched the service with three tiers in June 2022. On September 6, 2023, 12-month plans went up by $20 to $40 (Essential from $59.99 to $79.99 a year). On May 20, 2026, the 1- and 3-month plans went up for new subscribers: Essential to $10.99 a month, Extra to $16.99 and Premium to $19.99, while 12-month prices stayed where they were. Sony said existing subscribers keep their price unless "the existing subscription changes or lapses."

latest.what: 1-month and 3-month PlayStation Plus plans went up for new subscribers: Essential $9.99 to $10.99 a month ($24.99 to $27.99 for 3 months), Extra $14.99 to $16.99 ($39.99 to $43.99) and Premium $17.99 to $19.99 ($49.99 to $54.99). 12-month plans did not change.

PlayStation Plus.faq_up: Since the June 2022 relaunch, the 1-month Essential plan has gone from $9.99 to $10.99 (+10%), Extra from $14.99 to $16.99 and Premium from $17.99 to $19.99. The bigger jumps were on 12-month plans in September 2023: Essential $59.99 to $79.99 (+33%), Extra $99.99 to $134.99 (+35%) and Premium $119.99 to $159.99 (+33%).

Essential (1 month): Relaunch; same price as PlayStation Plus before
Essential (12 months): Relaunch; same price as PlayStation Plus before

notes: 3-month plans: Essential $24.99, Extra $39.99 and Premium $49.99 at the 2022 relaunch; since May 20, 2026 they are $27.99, $43.99 and $54.99.

Sony announced the May 2026 increase in a post on X on May 18, citing "ongoing market conditions" and naming only the Essential prices; Extra and Premium went up when the change took effect on May 20.

For the September 2023 increase, existing 12-month subscribers paid the old price until their first renewal on or after November 6, 2023; upgrades, downgrades or added time from September 6 used the new prices.
PlayStation's US PS Plus page on October 22, 2026 lists Essential at $10.99 / $27.99 / $79.99, Extra at $16.99 / $43.99 / $134.99 and Premium at $19.99 / $54.99 / $159.99 for 1, 3 and 12 months.
sources: Sony Interactive Entertainment press release, Jun 13, 2022 (US launch prices)
PlayStation Blog, Aug 30, 2023 (12-month price increase from Sep 6)
Polygon, May 21, 2026 (Extra and Premium also rose)

Verizon.name: Verizon
Verizon.title: Verizon fee history (2005–2026): the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge, from $0.40 to $4.69 a line
Verizon.desc: Every Verizon Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge increase: $0.40 a line in 2005, $1.95 in 2020, $3.30 in 2022, $3.78 now and $4.69 from Nov 15, 2026. Plus the Regulatory Charge rise to $0.26 on Nov 1. Dated and sourced.
Verizon.basis: Verizon's own flat per-line monthly surcharges on US postpaid mobile bills, in nominal dollars. These are Verizon charges, not taxes; the Federal Universal Service Charge, state fees and taxes come on top and vary by location. Compiled from Verizon's support pages, our daily snapshots of verizon.com/support/surcharges/, news reports and a 2022 class action complaint; last verified {verified}.
Verizon.intro: Verizon started adding an Administrative Charge to postpaid bills in September 2005 at $0.40 a line. It stayed under a dollar until December 2015, was renamed the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge in June 2022, and is $3.78 per voice line today. Verizon's Important Plan Information page says it rises to $4.69 on November 15, 2026, two weeks after the Regulatory Charge goes from $0.21 to $0.26. Together, the two flat charges go from $3.99 to $4.95 per voice line a month. The 3-year myPlan price lock doesn't cover them, because it excludes taxes, fees and surcharges.
Verizon.flagship: Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge (voice line)

latest.what: the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge is scheduled to rise from $3.78 to $4.69 per voice line a month (+$0.91, +24%), according to Verizon's Important Plan Information page (figures "as of October 1, 2026"). Data-only lines stay at $3.97. Two weeks earlier, on November 1, the Regulatory Charge goes from $0.21 to $0.26 per voice line.

Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge: Up from $0.95, the first time it topped a dollar

notes: Scheduled: the Regulatory Charge rises to $0.26 per voice line on November 1, 2026, and the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge to $4.69 per voice line on November 15, 2026. The tables will show them once they take effect.

Before 2015: the Administrative Charge started at $0.40 a line in September 2005, went to $0.70 in March 2007, and stayed under a dollar ($0.95 just before the increase) until December 2015, according to the 2022 Corsi v. Cellco class action complaint.
The 2022 Corsi v. Cellco class action over the charge was settled for $100 million; Verizon denied wrongdoing and said it would keep charging it and could raise it.
Verizon Home Internet isn't subject to these charges, and Verizon One plans include them in the plan price, according to Verizon's Important Plan Information page.
September 2025 dates come from Verizon's statement to Tom's Guide and The Verge that fee adjustments started in September; the exact day isn't confirmed.
sources: Verizon, Important Plan Information (as of Oct 1, 2026: $3.78, rising to $4.69 Nov 15; Regulatory Charge $0.21, rising to $0.26 Nov 1)
Verizon, Government taxes and fees and Verizon mobile surcharges (rename effective 6/3/22; Regulatory Charge to $0.26 Nov 1, 2026)
Corsi et al. v. Cellco Partnership, complaint filed Jul 18, 2022 (2005 to 2022 history)
The Verge, May 16, 2022 ($1.95 to $3.30 per voice line in June 2022)
The Verge, Dec 4, 2024 ($3.30 to $3.50 voice, $1.40 to $1.60 data, from Dec 18)
Tom's Guide, 2025 (September 2025: $3.50 to $3.78 voice, $1.60 to $3.97 data, Regulatory Charge $0.19 to $0.21)
Ars Technica, Jan 2024 (settlement notice: Verizon will keep charging the fee)
